In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the appetite-suppressing effect of GH is mediated by changes in hypothalamic monoamine and NPY concentrations, but that the mechanism of action of GH is independent of its effects as a repartitional agent.
GH has a direct and dose-dependent suppressive effect on FI and that this effect is mediated, at least in part, by changes in the hypothalamic concentrations of NPY mRNA.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the appetite-suppression effect of GH may not be a simple consequence of improved nutrient utilization.
GH may act to reduce FI by reducing NPY expression in the infundubular nuclei and midbrain.
GH may be an important regulator of appetite, and may be a useful tool to explore the mechanisms underlying appetite regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GH has an appetite-suppressive effect in juvenile broilers that is not dependent upon its repartitioning effects, and that this effect may involve alterations in hypothalamic NYP expression.
the appetite-suppressing effect of GH is dose-dependent and independent of its effects on growth and body composition.
